title: Engineering Ships From My Prototype Code
subtitle: The full loop, in one pair of hands — brief, design, prototype in code, ship

bio.short: I'm Tobias Treppmann, a product designer in Berlin. The work I do best has no handoff in it — the brief, the flow, the prototype in real code, the thing that ships. The last year went into AI running in production rather than AI that demos.
bio.long: The clearest thing to look at is the support copilot at Bibel TV. It drafts replies to viewer letters from the service handbook. Most of the design was deciding what it must not do. The system prompt carries an explicit restricted-topic list. It is manually operated and embedded in nothing, so a person has already read the letter before the model ever sees it and every send decision stays human. It went out fully optional, so it had to earn its place on the hard cases. The fundraising system I built alone, end to end: the performance analysis, the prompt architecture, an internal generation prototype, then the production skill whose output goes out across in-app notifications, web banners and video scripts. The practice underneath it is agentic engineering — I design in Figma, prototype in the target stack against real APIs, and engineering copies and adapts component structures, API calls and navigation patterns from that code into the production app. Engineering at Bibel TV is an external agency, so that handoff crosses a company boundary and holds anyway. Before that: at Ninox, freelance in summer 2025, I designed the prompt-to-database onboarding model with the CEO and technical co-founder — the generated schema renders into the real data-model editor rather than a chat preview, so a person can see and correct what the model produced. It became the basis for the public AI beta. At ChurchDesk I held product management and design at the same time, inherited a €20k client-funded booking project scoped internally as a standalone add-on module, reframed it into a platform capability and defended deep integration through the build: 70% less coordination time, 90% acceptance, then a rollout to the whole customer base. At Datameer, five years of data-dense interfaces for analysts inside banks and insurers, where the query-builder preview shows you a sample and the interface has to be honest about that without becoming unreadable.

context.company: Taxfix Group — consumer tax filing across Germany, Spain and the UK, brands Taxfix, Steuerbot and TaxScouts, based in Berlin. A product where getting it wrong has real financial and regulatory consequences for the person filing.
context.role: AI First Builder (Design) — full-loop ownership from user problem to shipped interface with as few handoffs as possible, working in a small pod alongside product and engineering. AI used to explore, prototype and accelerate, with taste as the editorial layer. First-principles interaction design rather than starting from the component library.
context.emphasis: Voice: first person, plain, practitioner rather than executive. Order to lead in: the AI work running in production at Bibel TV (a support copilot, a fundraising system built solo end to end, agentic engineering); then the Ninox prompt-to-database onboarding model; then the ChurchDesk booking outcome with its numbers. Berlin-based, German native, English C2.
